testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If the ABS light comes on while driving, what does it mean?

options.text: The ABS cannot work because of weather.
The ABS just activated.
The ABS is not working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: The ABS warning light means something in the Anti-Lock Braking System is not working properly.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning comes on in a vehicle with air brakes, what should you do?

options.text: Test the brakes while driving and continue if they seem okay.
Stop driving immediately.
Turn on the hazard lights and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop driving immediately.
questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning comes on, stop the vehicle and park it safely as soon as possible. You need to keep some brake power to stop safely.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, what is true about the air tanks?

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You choose which system to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. They share the same controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: How far does an air brake vehicle need to stop from 55 mph under ideal conditions?

options.text: 300 feet
100 feet
450 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 450 feet
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. An air brake vehicle traveling at 55 mph needs about 450 feet to stop under ideal conditions.

questions.question: How do you stop a vehicle with air brakes?

options.text: Press the brake pedal down.
Lift the brake pedal up.
Pull out the air brake knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal down.
questions.explanation: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, simply press the brake pedal down.

questions.question: What happens when brakes are out of adjustment?

options.text: They work properly.
Some brakes overwork and break down.
The vehicle accelerates better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Some brakes overwork and break down.
questions.explanation: Out-of-adjustment brakes fail faster than properly adjusted ones. Check brake adjustment often to prevent brake problems.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, when does air pressure move the rods and slack adjusters?

options.text: When the driver presses the brake pedal.
When the driver uses the emergency brake.
When the driver uses the trailer hand valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the driver presses the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. The air pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: What does an air brake system use to make brakes work?

options.text: Compressed air
Outside air
Non-compressed air

questions.correctAnswerText: Compressed air
questions.explanation: Large vehicles use air brakes. An air brake system uses compressed air to operate.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in an air brake system is releasing air, what does this mean?

options.text: This is normal and you should not worry.
Something is wrong with the brakes.
The valve is working correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if system pressure gets too high. If it releases air, something is wrong. Have a mechanic fix it.

questions.question: What should happen before air pressure drops below 55 psi in an air brake system?

options.text: The warning light should turn on.
The vehicle will get stuck in gear.
The front lights should flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: The warning light should turn on.
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light must turn on before pressure drops below 55 psi. If the warning light does not work during inspection, the vehicle is not safe to drive.

questions.question: Do not drive a vehicle if any brake drum has a crack larger than ____ of the friction area width.

options.text: One half
One third
One fifth

questions.correctAnswerText: One half
questions.explanation: Check the brake drums during your walk-around inspection before driving. It is unsafe to drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: Foundation brakes are used:

options.text: Only on the front wheels.
Only on the rear wheels.
On all wheels of a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all wheels of a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are used on all wheels. The most common type is the s-cam drum brake.

questions.question: While driving, ____ holds spring brakes in place.

options.text: Air pressure
Electricity
Gasoline

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure
questions.explanation: Air pressure keeps spring brakes in place while driving. If air pressure gets too low, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: You should test the low pressure warning signal by:

options.text: Turning on the engine and applying the trailer hand brake.
Pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly several times.
Removing wheel chocks and disengaging the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly several times.
questions.explanation: Test the low pressure warning light after the system charges. Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times. This releases air from the system. The warning signal should turn on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: Having ABS on only one axle:

options.text: Can be dangerous.
Still gives you better control when braking.
Slows the vehicle but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still gives you better control when braking.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) on only one axle, you still have more control when braking than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle unattended:

options.text: Always use the parking brake.
Use the parking brake only if parked on a slope.
Do not use the parking brake because it can damage the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when parking. However, do not use it if the brakes are very hot or if brakes are wet and the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: During an inspection, slack adjusters on S-cam brakes should not move more than:

options.text: One foot.
One centimeter.
One inch.

questions.correctAnswerText: One inch.
questions.explanation: Park on level ground and set wheel chocks. Pull each slack adjuster to check it does not move more than one inch. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: Some air brake systems add alcohol to:

options.text: Stop the brakes from squeaking.
Prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
Prevent people from breathing air from the system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to help prevent ice formation in cold weather.

questions.question: A wig wag is:

options.text: A low pressure warning device.
A tube that carries air to the brakes.
A type of air brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: A low pressure warning device.
questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into your view if air pressure drops between 55 and 75 psi.

questions.question: When driving down a steep downgrade:

options.text: Use the air brakes.
Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking.
Downshift instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On long or steep downgrades, use engine braking to control your speed. Use the brakes only to help with engine braking.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air storage tanks?

options.text: They are not allowed on vehicles.
They store compressed air for the brakes.
They should be emptied of air after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: They store compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks in an air brake system hold compressed air that the brakes use. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of air tanks.

questions.question: What gauge shows how much air pressure is in your vehicle's tanks?

options.text: The supply pressure gauge
The ABS malfunction lamp
The tractor protection valve

questions.correctAnswerText: The supply pressure gauge
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge tells the driver how much air pressure is in the air tanks.

questions.question: What should you do if the low air pressure warning signal comes on?

options.text: Keep driving, but repair the brakes within a week.
Pull over safely and check the brakes.
Call a mechanic while you are driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over safely and check the brakes.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on while driving a vehicle with air brakes, stop the vehicle safely as soon as you can while you still have brake control. Check and repair the brakes right away.

questions.question: What color light shows that a vehicle's ABS is not working?

options.text: Green
Blue
Yellow

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) use a yellow warning light to tell the driver that the ABS is not working properly.

questions.question: What does an application pressure gauge measure?

options.text: How much air pressure is being used on the brakes right now.
How much air pressure is stored and ready to use.
How much air pressure is needed to stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being used on the brakes right now.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle has an application pressure gauge, it shows how much air pressure is being used on the brakes at that moment. This gauge helps drivers see if their brakes are starting to wear out.
